card.name: Enantiomer and racemic drug relationships
card.fires_on: Words just before or inside the term enantiomer or isomer, when a label says one drug is the R or S form of another. Also fires inside names like arformoterol that point to a racemic parent drug.

modes.label: Before enantiomer
modes.description: Small words or letters like the, an, R, or S right before the word enantiomer.
modes.example: Dexlansoprazole is the<< R>>-enantiomer of lansopraz

modes.label: Inside enantiomer or isomer
modes.description: Pieces of the words enantiomer or isomers being spelled out.

modes.label: Single-isomer drug names
modes.description: Partway through a name of a single-isomer drug that has a racemic parent.

card.writes: It promotes stereo-chemistry words like cis, stereo, and rac, so the model expects enantiomer or racemic terms.
card.plain: It marks spots where a label says a drug is a mirror-image form of another drug.
